title: Finding the commit that broke checkout
subtitle: Letting git bisect search a hundred commits in seven steps

scenes.narration: Checkout totals were right last Monday and wrong today, with a hundred and twenty commits in between. Git can search those commits for us, halving the list each time.
scenes.summary: Find the one commit, out of **120**, that broke the checkout total
bullets: Last Monday's release, v4.2, was fine

scenes.title: git bisect
scenes.narration: Here is the whole search, run in the shop's code.

entries.output: Bisecting: 60 revisions left to test after this (roughly 6 steps)

entries.command: git bisect run pnpm test test/checkout.test.ts
entries.output:
[FAIL]{bad} totals include shipping once
Bisecting: 29 revisions left to test after this (roughly 5 steps)
[PASS]{good} totals include shipping once
Bisecting: 14 revisions left to test after this (roughly 4 steps)
…
==3f9c2e1== is the first bad commit
    Apply free-shipping discount per item

steps.say: We tell git which commit is bad and which was good. It picks the commit halfway between.
Then git runs the checkout test at each stop by itself. Here the test fails, so the bug is in the older half.
At the next stop the test passes, so the bug is in the newer half of what is left.
Seven test runs later, git names the first bad commit, the free shipping discount.
That commit touched one file, the shipping code, so that is where to look.
